Campaign notes:
- Four angles are legally approved: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- Across the first 10 pushes, 5 landed (+0.50 aggregate outcome). No per-day or angle-level performance breakdown is available, so do not infer that B or D caused the result.
- B (quality story) and D (customer testimonial) were selected repeatedly as durable, lower-pressure approaches. A and C have not been tested in this run.
- Two unsubscribes were reported via support on some days and processed; they cannot be attributed to a specific angle.
- No deliverability complaints were reported on several days.
- For future decisions, prioritize clean experimentation: rotate or A/B test angles while recording angle-level outcomes, unsubscribes, and deliverability. Avoid treating queued pushes or zero day-level outcomes as evidence of success or failure.

Campaign notes:
- Four legally approved angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- First 10 pushes: 5 landed, aggregate outcome +0.50. Latest report for the next 10 pushes (Days 11–20): 4 landed, aggregate outcome +0.40. Neither report provides per-day or angle-level results, so do not attribute performance to any angle.
- Days 11–20 composition: A was used 8 times; C was used twice (Days 14 and 16); B and D were not used in this segment. Most entries were queued with zero immediate outcome, which is not evidence of success or failure.
- No deliverability complaints were reported on several mornings. Two unsubscribes were previously reported through support and processed; neither can be tied to an angle.
- Creative refreshes, list growth, and legal approval are contextual factors, not evidence of performance.
- Future runs should balance or randomize angle assignments and record, per push, angle, conversions/outcome, unsubscribes, deliverability, and creative version. Continue testing B and D alongside A and C rather than inferring winners from aggregate reports.

Campaign notes:
- Four legally approved angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- First 10 pushes: 5 landed, aggregate outcome +0.50. Days 11–20: 4 landed, aggregate +0.40. Days 21–30: 7 of 10 landed, aggregate +0.70. None of these reports includes per-day or angle-level results, so do not attribute performance to any angle.
- Days 11–20 used A eight times and C twice (Days 14 and 16); B and D were not used. Days 21–30 used D once (Day 21) and B nine times (Days 22–30). This is heavily imbalanced and cannot establish B as a winner.
- Most queued pushes initially show zero immediate outcome; this is not evidence of success or failure. Day 30’s +0.70 is a pooled report for the prior 10 pushes, not a Day 30 result.
- No deliverability complaints were reported on several mornings. Two unsubscribes were reported via support and processed; neither is attributable to an angle. List growth, banner/creative refreshes, legal approval, and send timing are contextual factors, not performance evidence.
- Continue balanced or randomized assignment across A–D. Record for every push: angle, creative version, conversions/outcome, unsubscribes, deliverability, and relevant audience/list details. Await per-push results before drawing conclusions; continue testing all four angles rather than inferring winners from aggregate reports.

Campaign notes:
- Four legally approved angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- Historical pooled results: pushes 1–10: 5 landed, +0.50; 11–20: 4 landed, +0.40; 21–30: 7/10 landed, +0.70. Day 40 report: 2/10 landed, +0.20. None has per-day or angle-level detail; do not attribute pooled results to individual days or angles.
- Days 11–20 were heavily A-weighted (A eight, C two); days 21–30 heavily B-weighted (B nine, D one), so those periods cannot establish winners.
- Days 31–40 used D seven times (31, 33, 35–38, 40) and C three times (32, 34, 39); A and B were not used. This is also imbalanced and provides no reliable comparison. Most individual outcomes remain pending/zero at queue time.
- Day 37’s two support-reported unsubscribes were processed but are not attributable to an angle. No deliverability complaints were reported in the noted period.
- Banner refreshes, list growth, legal approval, and normal 10am timing are contextual factors, not performance evidence. Record creative/banner version and audience/list context with each push.
- Continue balanced or randomized assignment across A–D. For every push, record angle, creative version, conversions/outcome, unsubscribes, deliverability, and audience/list details. Await per-push results and avoid treating pooled reports or queued zeroes as angle evidence.

Campaign notes:
- Four legally approved angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- Historical pooled results: pushes 1–10: 5 landed, +0.50; 11–20: 4/10, +0.40; 21–30: 7/10, +0.70; day-40 report: 2/10, +0.20. Day-50 report: 6/10, +0.60. These reports lack per-day and angle-level detail; do not attribute pooled results to individual days or angles.
- Days 11–20 were A-heavy (A eight, C two); days 21–30 B-heavy (B nine, D one); days 31–40 D-heavy (D seven, C three). None establishes an angle winner.
- Days 41–50 were highly imbalanced: A seven (41, 44–46, 48–50), B two (42, 47), C one (43), D zero. This provides no reliable comparison and does not support claims that A performs better.
- Most individual outcomes remain queued/zero at queue time. Await per-push results; queued zeroes are not evidence.
- Day 37’s two support-reported unsubscribes were processed but are not attributable to an angle. No deliverability complaints were reported in the noted period.
- List growth occurred on several days. Banner art refreshed on days 43, 48, 49, and 50. Legal approval and normal 10am timing are contextual factors, not performance evidence.
- Continue balanced or randomized assignment across A–D. For every push, record angle, creative/banner version, audience/list context, conversions/outcome, unsubscribes, and deliverability. Analyze only after per-push results are available.

Campaign notes:
- Four legally approved angles: A) price cut, B) quality story, C) limited-time urgency, D) customer testimonial.
- Historical pooled results: pushes 1–10: 5/10, +0.50; 11–20: 4/10, +0.40; 21–30: 7/10, +0.70; day-40 report: 2/10, +0.20; day-50 report: 6/10, +0.60; day-60 report: 2/10, +0.20. Reports lack per-day and angle-level detail; never attribute pooled results to individual days or angles.
- Days 11–20 were A-heavy; 21–30 B-heavy; 31–40 D-heavy. Days 41–50 were A-heavy (A7, B2, C1, D0), providing no reliable angle comparison.
- Days 51–60 were exclusively D. The day-60 pooled result therefore does not establish D’s performance.
- Queued/zero outcomes are not evidence; await per-push results before analysis.
- Support-reported unsubscribes occurred on days 37, 52, and 57; processed but not attributable to an angle. No deliverability complaints were reported on days 51, 54, or 60, and none were noted elsewhere in the period.
- Legal approval, normal 10am timing, list growth (day 59), and banner refresh (day 58; also 43, 48–50) are contextual factors, not performance evidence.
- Resume balanced or randomized assignment across A–D. Record for every push: angle, creative/banner version, audience/list context, conversions/outcome, unsubscribes, and deliverability. Analyze only when per-push results are available.
